messages.content:
The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-10T22:51:12Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-10T22:51:38Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. Its condition looks back over 1 minute {rule_looks_back}.
Not broken: the alarm was disproven - no minute of the window Argus read departed from the service's baseline, so there is no onset, duration or impact to report.
Argus held the incident for 19 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-10T22:51:52Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-10T22:51:33Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-10T22:51:36Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-10T22:51:36Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-10T22:51:47Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 22:51:12 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-10T22:51:51Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 360 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-10T22:51:52Z {T6.1} Argus: Nothing in the window matched the alarm's own claim - Error rate above threshold for 5m {T6.2} - in errors, p50, p95, p99, memory or the alert rule's series, over 360 {T6.3} minutes read between 16:52 {T6.4} and 22:51 {T6.5}. The rule fired rather than the service failing
  - [T7] 2026-11-10T22:51:52Z {T7.1} Argus: Moved the incident to DISPROVEN - the alarm's own claim was not in the window

Changes to production it read:
  - Deploys not read; flags not read.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - Not read.

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - none

Actions it took:
  - none

Action items the record already holds:
  - none

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: The evidence does not show why the HighErrorRate rule fired: no minute of the window read, including the rule's own series, departed from the service's baseline. So the record shows no failure mechanism behind the alarm.
cause_in_plain_words: An error alarm for the shop service went off even though the service's own measurements showed nothing wrong, and the record does not show why the alarm went off.
still_at_risk: The same alarm could fire again while the service is working normally.
symptom: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; an error-rate alarm fired with no matching errors
causal_chain 1: Nobody using io-shop was seen to have any problem. What was seen instead was the HighErrorRate alarm saying the error rate was above its threshold, while the metrics read showed no such errors. (cites AL1; T6, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 2: The rule fired but the service did not fail: across errors, p50, p95, p99, memory and the alert rule's own series, no minute of the window read departed from baseline. The record does not show why the rule fired. Deploys and flags were not read, so no change was tied to the alarm and none was ruled out. (cites T5, under "What Argus did, in order"; T6, under "What Argus did, in order")
action_items 1: Look into the HighErrorRate rule for io-shop and find out why it fired when its own series, as read, showed no departure from baseline.
action_items 2: Decide whether HighErrorRate on io-shop should page on-call. If it should, link the rule to an on-call paging route.
went_wrong 1: The alert was not linked to an on-call incident, so nobody was paged by it.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
